extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (appellants/attorneys) involved in ex parte appeals to the USPTO Board
extracted.subtask_short: ex parte appeal briefing and remand
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for reply briefs, substitute examiner's answers, remands, oral hearings, fees, and Board jurisdiction in USPTO ex parte appeals. Covers timing, contents, ramifications, and examiner/Board actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief timing (37 CFR 41.41(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file only a single reply brief within the later of two months from the date of either the examiner's answer, or a decision refusing to grant a petition under § 1.181 to designate a new ground of rejection in an examiner's answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time to file the reply brief may be granted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(b) (for patent applications) or 1.550(c) (for ex parte reexamination proceedings). Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not permitted. If no reply brief is filed within the two-month period, the application will normally be forwarded to the Board for decision on the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief content prohibition (37 CFR 41.41(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.116 for amendments/affidavits/evidence filed after final action but before/on date of filing appeal, and 37 CFR 41.33 for such items filed after the date of filing the appeal. Any new amendment must be submitted in papers separate from the reply brief; a paper containing an amendment is not a reply brief within 37 CFR 41.41.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief argument limitations (37 CFR 41.41(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any argument raised in the reply brief which was not raised in the appeal brief, or is not responsive to an argument raised in the examiner's answer, including any designated new ground of rejection, will not be considered by the Board for purposes of the present appeal, unless good cause is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments must be responsive and should address issues raised in the examiner's answer or be shown to have good cause to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a reply brief is required to maintain the appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply brief is required to maintain the appeal when responding to: (A) an examiner's answer that designates a new ground of rejection pursuant to 37 CFR 41.39; or (B) a substitute examiner’s answer responding to a remand by the Board for further consideration of a rejection pursuant to 37 CFR 41.50(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant fails to file the required reply brief or a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 within two months from mailing of such an examiner's answer or substitute examiner’s answer, the appeal may be dismissed. The reply brief must address each new ground of rejection set forth in the answer in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief format and required pages (37 CFR 41.37(c) guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reply brief should include the following items, with each item starting on a separate page: (A) Identification page (appellant's name(s), application number, filing date, title of invention, name of examiner, art unit, and title 'Reply Brief'); (B) Argument page(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each item should start on a separate page to follow requirements of a brief as set forth in 37 CFR 41.37(c). New or non-admitted affidavits and other evidence are not permitted in a reply brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing an amendment/affidavit/evidence with a reply brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reply brief accompanied by an amendment, affidavit or other evidence will be treated as a request that prosecution be reopened before the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such papers must be separate from the reply brief and are subject to entry provisions of 37 CFR 41.33 and related rules. A paper containing an amendment is not a reply brief and will not be entitled to entry simply because characterized as a reply brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolling and petitions to designate new ground (37 CFR 41.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to seek review of the primary examiner’s failure to designate a rejection as a new ground of rejection must be by petition to the Director under § 1.181 filed within two months from the entry of the examiner’s answer and before filing any reply brief; failure to timely file constitutes waiver of such arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition is granted, a two-month period is provided to file a reply under § 1.111 to reopen prosecution; failure to timely file causes dismissal. If petition is refused, a two-month period is provided to file only a single reply brief under § 41.41. Filing a reply brief while a petition is pending will be treated as withdrawal of the petition if within two months from the examiner's answer and before a decision on the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to reply to a substitute examiner’s answer under 37 CFR 41.50(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to timely file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or a reply brief in response to a substitute examiner’s answer written in response to a remand by the Board for further consideration of a rejection under 37 CFR 41.50(a), the appeal will be sua sponte dismissed as to the claims subject to the rejection for which the Board has remanded the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all claims under appeal are subject to the rejection, the entire appeal will be dismissed. If only some claims are subject, dismissal operates as authorization to cancel those claims and the appeal continues as to remaining claims. Examiner should follow MPEP § 1215 after dismissal (e.g., abandonment if no allowed claim).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute examiner's answer on remand not for further consideration of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board remands an application to the examiner for reasons not for further consideration of a rejection (e.g., to consider an IDS filed before Board jurisdiction, a reply brief raising new issues, an amendment, or an affidavit), the examiner may provide a substitute examiner’s answer and appellant may respond by filing a reply brief within two months from the mailing of the substitute answer. Appellant may not request reopening under 37 CFR 41.50(a)(2)(i) unless the remand is for further consideration of a rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of any IDS or petition filed while Board has jurisdiction will be held in abeyance until Board's jurisdiction ends. Appellant is not required to reply to substitute answer when remand is not for further consideration of a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal forwarding fee requirement (37 CFR 41.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must pay the appeal forwarding fee set forth in § 37 CFR 41.20(b)(4) within the later of two months from the date of either the examiner's answer, or a decision refusing to grant a petition under § 1.181 to designate a new ground of rejection. Failure to pay within the period specified results in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions under § 1.136(a) are not applicable. The examiner's answer should notify that the fee must be paid or appeal will be dismissed. The fee requirement was added March 19, 2013; waiver exists where appeal brief fee was paid before that date under specified circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for oral hearing timing and form (37 CFR 41.47(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant desires an oral hearing, appellant must file, as a separate paper captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING,' a written request accompanied by the fee within two months from the date of the examiner's answer or on the date of filing of a reply brief, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/32 may be used. Time period may only be extended by filing under 37 CFR 1.136(b) or 1.550(c) as applicable. If request is not filed in a separate paper captioned correctly, the request is improper and case assigned on briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of not timely requesting oral hearing (37 CFR 41.47(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If no request and fee for oral hearing have been timely filed, the appeal will be assigned for consideration and decision on the briefs without an oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely and proper filing is required to preserve the hearing; improper captioning or missing fee renders the request improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing time limits and allocation (37 CFR 41.47(d)/(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an oral hearing is held, oral argument will ordinarily be limited to twenty minutes for appellant and fifteen minutes for the primary examiner unless otherwise ordered. Appellant will argue first and may reserve time for rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional time is necessary, appellant should file a request in a separate paper addressed to the Clerk of the Board well in advance; Board/senior panel member has discretion to grant extra time. Appellant may use unused allotted time for rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing evidence and argument limitations (37 CFR 41.47(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: At the oral hearing, appellant may only rely on evidence that has been previously entered and considered by the primary examiner and present arguments that have been relied upon in the brief or reply brief, except upon a showing of good cause where new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of either the Board or a Federal Court may be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiner may likewise rely only on argument and evidence relied upon in an answer except as permitted for new arguments under good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board discretion to deny or cancel oral hearing (37 CFR 41.47(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding submission of a proper request, if the Board decides that a hearing is not necessary, the Board will notify appellant and decide on the briefs. Examples include when the Board is convinced prior to hearing that the examiner's position cannot be sustained or when the Director orders a remand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board will notify appellant if hearing is deemed unnecessary; no refund of the hearing fee if appellant fails to confirm or appear; failure to confirm the hearing within required time results in waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public attendance and decorum for oral hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the public may attend oral hearings in appeals of reexamination proceedings, reissues, and published applications; members of the public are not permitted to attend appeals of non-published applications. All parties should follow published Hearing Room Protocol/Decorum; appropriate attire is clothing for an important business meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More information available at USPTO hearings web page. Appellant should notify Board early of plans to waive or change hearing to avoid wasted resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner participation in oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the primary examiner wishes to appear and present oral argument, the examiner must request the opportunity in a separate letter on form PTOL-90 using form paragraph 12.279.03. If the appellant appears, the examiner will generally be allowed 15 minutes to reply and present a statement setting forth the examiner's position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner generally may rely on argument and evidence in the examiner's answer, but may rely on a new argument based on a recent relevant decision of the Board or Federal Court. The examiner should notify the usher and indicate intention to participate on the day of the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board jurisdiction start and end (37 CFR 41.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction over the proceeding passes to the Board upon the filing of a reply brief under § 41.41 or the expiration of the time in which to file such a reply brief, whichever is earlier. Jurisdiction ends when (1) Director/Board enters a remand order, (2) Board enters a final decision and judicial review is sought or time expires, (3) an express abandonment complying with § 1.138 is recognized, (4) a request for continued examination complying with § 1.114 is filed, (5) appellant fails to take required action under specified rules and Board dismisses, or (6) appellant reopens prosecution pursuant to § 41.40(b) or in response to a new ground in a Board decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment or paper relating to the appeal filed after jurisdiction passes but prior to Board decision may be considered by the examiner only if case is remanded for that purpose. Jurisdiction passes from Technology Centers to the Board at time specified in 37 CFR 41.35(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents filed during Board jurisdiction are held in abeyance (37 CFR 41.35(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for petitions authorized by this part, consideration of any information disclosure statement or petition filed while the Board possesses jurisdiction over the proceeding will be held in abeyance until the Board's jurisdiction ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants and examiners should be aware that filings made while Board has jurisdiction may not be acted upon until jurisdiction ends; plan submissions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant options after Board remand for further consideration of rejection (37 CFR 41.50(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: When remanded by the Board for further consideration of a rejection, the appellant must within two months either (A) reopen prosecution by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 with or without amendment/affidavit/other evidence (to be entered if relevant), or (B) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief as provided in 37 CFR 41.41. A reply brief accompanied by amendment/affidavit/evidence will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) do not apply to the two-month period; use 1.136(b) for authorized extensions. Failure to exercise one of the options will lead to sua sponte dismissal as to the remanded claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and approval requirements for substitute examiner's answer on remand (form ¶ 12.285 and approval notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute Examiner's Answer on remand for further consideration of a rejection should use the prescribed form paragraph (¶ 12.285) and must include the substitute answer reasons. A Technology Center Director or designee must approve every substitute examiner's answer (signature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: insert date of remand, provide reasons supporting the rejections, and insert TC Director signature. Supervisory patent examiner must approve actions withdrawing a final rejection and reopening prosecution to enter a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand to consider amendments or affidavits/declarations (limits) (MPEP § 1211.02 & § 1211.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Board has no obligation to consider new or amended claims filed while it has jurisdiction. A proposed amendment filed after filing of a brief to cancel claims (where cancellation does not affect other claims) or to rewrite dependent claims into independent form may be remanded. Affidavits or declarations filed with a notice of appeal but before jurisdiction may be considered for entry only upon necessary showings under 37 CFR 1.116(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposed amendment that is effectively an abandonment of the appeal will normally result in dismissal by the Board. Affidavits/declarations filed after notice of appeal but before jurisdiction may be considered by examiner only if they overcome all rejections and show good and sufficient reasons for late presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand for further search should be rare and require minimal search standard (MPEP § 1211.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: It should be extremely rare for the Board to remand a case to the examiner for further search. When necessary, the Board should conduct a search (on-line or otherwise) of at least one subclass and cite art from that subclass to demonstrate the basis on which it concludes a search of this area would be material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A remand to the examiner extends pendency and may necessitate patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b). The art cited to justify remand need not be art upon which a rejection can be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may require additional briefing/information (37 CFR 41.50(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may order appellant to additionally brief any matter it considers helpful in reaching a reasoned decision on the appeal and will set a time period to respond; failure to timely comply may result in sua sponte dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include applicability of particular case law or prior art not previously identified. Extensions of time are available only under 37 CFR 1.136(b). Consideration of IDSs filed during Board jurisdiction is held in abeyance.
